hook_text: On top of one mountain, rivers begin that flow to two different oceans.
clip_script: Mont-aux-Sources, the Drakensberg, more than three thousand metres high. Little streams trickle out of wet, spongy grass. This is where rivers begin, at their source. One stream, the young Thukela, plunges over the cliff in the Tugela Falls, one of the highest in the world, and flows east to the Indian Ocean. Other streams flow west, and their water joins the Gariep, all the way to the Atlantic. Rivers always flow downhill, from source to mouth.
visual_style: Whiteboard mountain plateau with little streams joining, a waterfall pouring over a cliff, and arrows to two oceans.
mood: Fresh and awe-filled, like standing where rivers are born.
pacing: Slow trickle at the source, a dramatic plunge, then a long flow to the sea.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and trace one river near you from source to mouth.
